props.title: The Last of Us

sections.content: The post-apocalyptic journey of Joel and Ellie captivated both gamers and TV audiences, but Children of Men (2006) pioneered many of the same emotional beats and survival horror elements years earlier. Alfonso Cuarón's masterpiece follows Clive Owen protecting humanity's last hope through a decaying civilization, much like Joel's mission. The raw father-daughter dynamic found in The Road (2009) offers an even closer parallel, with Viggo Mortensen guiding his son through a collapsed world while fighting off infected humans.

sections.content: The fungal infection premise draws clear inspiration from zombie classics, but with a scientific twist that 28 Days Later (2002) similarly employed. Danny Boyle's infected humans brought a terrifying speed and ferocity that influenced both the game and show's Runners. Train to Busan (2016) later perfected this formula of protecting loved ones while navigating through hordes of infected, all while maintaining intense emotional stakes.

The found family theme resonates strongly with Logan (2017), where a gruff protector must escort a special young girl across dangerous territory. Both stories examine how trauma shapes relationships and the cost of violence on the human psyche. **Mad Max: Fury Road** (2015) shares this DNA - a hardened survivor reluctantly joining forces with others while racing across a hostile landscape. sections.content: The survival horror elements draw from films like **I Am Legend** (2007), where isolation and monster-filled darkness create constant tension. **A Quiet Place** (2018) similarly masters the art of silence as survival, much like the game's stealth mechanics against Clickers. Both properties understand that true horror comes from the threat to loved ones rather than just jump scares.
